residencyRequirements.description: Petitioner must be an actual and bona fide resident of the county where the petition is filed for at least 90 days before filing. (Utah Code § 81-4-402, effective 9/1/2024; formerly § 30-3-1)

waitingPeriod.description: The court may not enter a decree of divorce until 30 days after the day on which the petition is filed, unless the court finds that extraordinary circumstances exist. (Utah Code § 81-4-402, effective 9/1/2024; formerly § 30-3-18)

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: Irreconcilable differences causing irremediable breakdown of the marriage

fault.name: Impotency
fault.description: Impotency of the respondent at the time of marriage

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: Adultery committed by the respondent subsequent to marriage

fault.name: Willful Desertion
fault.description: Willful desertion of the petitioner for more than one year

fault.name: Willful Neglect
fault.description: Willful neglect of the respondent to provide for the petitioner the common necessaries of life

fault.name: Cruel Treatment
fault.description: Cruel treatment of the petitioner by the respondent to the extent of causing bodily injury or great mental distress

fault.name: Incurable Insanity
fault.description: Permanent insanity of the respondent for a period of at least three years

fault.name: Living Separate and Apart
fault.description: Parties have lived separately under a decree of separate maintenance for three consecutive years without cohabitation

propertyDivision.description: Utah is an equitable distribution state. The court divides marital property in a manner that is fair and equitable, considering the parties' circumstances. There is no fixed formula or presumption of equal division.

factors: Financial condition and needs of receiving spouse
Ability of paying spouse to provide support
Whether receiving spouse has custody of minor children
Whether receiving spouse worked in business owned by paying spouse
Whether receiving spouse contributed to paying spouse's education
Fault of the parties (in certain circumstances)
